text.p: These are the leading stories in the Pakistani press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The Privatisation Commission has received a legal notice from Saudi Basharahil Ltd challenging the state commission's decision to cancel a deal to sell a 26 percent stake in state-run United Bank of Ltd.
- Pakistan State Oil has earned after-tax profit of 1.499 billion rupees in 1995/96 (July-June) against a profit of 1.042 billion rupees last year.
- The trade deficit is expected to narrow to $2.016 billion in 1996/97 (July-June), with exports totalling $9.965 billion and imports $11.981 billion.
- The World Bank has approved financing worth $30.9 million for Southern Electric Power Co Ltd.
- The Privatisation Commission has appointed N.M. Rothschild and First Capital Security as financial advisors for the privatisation of state-run Sui Northern Gas Pipelines Ltd.
- Afghanistan's northern warlord General Abdul Rasheed Dostum has invited all political and religious groups, except the Islamic Taleban militia, to Mazar-i-Sharif for talks aimed at ending fighting.
- The Lahore High Court has reinstated the ousted chief minister Manzoor Wattoo, asking him to show his majority in the provincial assembly within 10 days.

- The All Pakistan Textile Mills Association would appeal to the European Commission, instead of the World Trade Organisation, if anti-dumping duties were imposed on Pakistani loom-made unbleached cotton fabrics by the European Commission's anti-dumping committee.
- Indua Motor Company Ltd, a joint venture between Habib Group of Industries and Toyota Motor Co of Japan, proposes to start manufacture-cum-assembly of 800-1,000 cc cars in Pakistan.
- Tea manufacturing companies have decided to increase the prices of their products because of the sharp devaluation of the Pakistani rupee against the dollar.
- Emirates Bank intends to expand its services in Pakistan by venturing into leasing, insurance and stock brokering.
